To the Semi-Centennial Convention with the Theta Chapter, 1883
Sing for my sake the old refrain:
Then till the sands of life are run,
We'll sing to thee Psi Upsilon,
Long live Psi Upsilon! Psi Upsilon!
-Chester A. Arthur, Theta 1848

At the Convention of 1929, with the Eta, held in Washington
Twenty-seven chapters! That combines a force that rightly directed will mean much
for the progress of our country. They represent the character of men that we need; men
who are intellectual, who are strong, who are loyal, who have high ideals and have
courage, have comradeship and are for the public and the country all the time, without
talking about it. That last is exceptional. I am glad and proud to belong to it.
-William H. Taft, Beta 1878
